scope: Segment 120 field-level rules, serialization, applicability, and companion-segment/ordering boundary within Data Section 3 of a Financial Transaction Response
extractionEvidence: regression-artifact-validator/docs/specs/extracted_text.txt lines 13753-13792 (Section 12.18); docs/atl105_complete_templates.json message_templates['Financial Transaction Response'] and ['EMV Financial Transaction Response']

rules.title: Segment Length is present, exactly 4 digits (zero-padded), and equals the segment's actual encoded length including the Segment Type field and Field Separators
Print Data is required and must be present whenever Segment 120 is included

Print Data must not exceed 999 characters AND total serialized Segment 120 length (Segment Type + Segment Length + Print Data + separators) must not exceed 1,009 alphanumeric characters -- both caps enforced independently
Exactly one Field Separator appears between Field 1 and Field 2, and exactly one between Field 2 and Field 3; there is no trailing separator after Print Data
Segment 120 is present only in Financial Transaction Response and EMV Financial Transaction Response messages; it must not appear on a request message
Segment 120 is the final segment of the Data Section 3 companion sequence in a Financial Transaction Response / EMV Financial Transaction Response
Print Data may contain '\' as a line delimiter between lines of receipt text for Blackhawk phone activation/recharge

provisionalItems.question: BR-263-2 (page 263) states Segment 120 'always appears at the end' of a Financial Transaction Response, and the AI Solution generated a dedicated test (SC-1839 / TC-4305, TC-4306) asserting exactly that. However docs/atl105_complete_templates.json lists Segment 120 as the 3rd of 9 segments in the Financial Transaction Response template (and 3rd of 10 in the EMV Financial Transaction Response template), ahead of Segments 134, 136, 146, 148, 152, and 155.
provisionalItems.resolution: The AI-generated template's segment order (112, 115, 120, 134, 136, 146, 148, 152, 155 -- and the EMV variant with 131 inserted) is in STRICT ASCENDING SEGMENT-NUMBER order in both templates. No other spec section documents true field-by-field wire order for these response messages; this ordering matches the pattern of the spec's own 'Alphabetical List of Data Element Names' cross-reference appendix, which groups segments by number, not transmission order. This is assessed as a numeric-sort artifact of AI extraction, not evidence of true wire order. The literal, first-party spec statement (BR-263-2) is therefore treated as authoritative: Segment 120 is the final segment of Data Section 3. SEG120-R-007 is now hard-enforced when an explicit segment order is available in test data.

provisionalItems.question: Should Segment Length always be serialized zero-padded to exactly 4 digits, or does it vary between 3 and 4 digits depending on value?
provisionalItems.resolution: regression-artifact-validator/docs/specs/extracted_text.txt lines 21313-21340 (Element 84, Segment Length, page 13-66/399) explicitly states: 'Segment Length has a length of four digits in the following seven instances only: EBT Data Segment (No. 103), SKU Data Segment (No. 114), Print Data Segment (No. 115), Proprietary Data Load Segment (No. 118), Print Data 2 Segment (No. 120), EMV Request Data Segment (No.130), EMV Response Data Segment (No. 131)' and 'It cannot have a length of 4 digits when sending any other segment.' Segment 120's Segment Length is therefore ALWAYS exactly 4 digits, zero-padded (e.g. '0024', '1009'). BR-400-18's '001-1009' rendering is a lossy simplification of the true zero-padded 4-digit range by the AI extraction pipeline, not evidence of variable width.

provisionalItems.question: The field table lists Print Data's own max length as 999, but 1,009 (total) minus 3 (Segment Type) minus 4 (Segment Length, now confirmed fixed-width) minus 2 (separators) = 1,000, not 999 -- a 1-character arithmetic gap between the per-field cap and the total-segment cap. Is 999 a typo for 1,000, is the total cap actually 1,010 (matching the SKU Data Segment's analogous 4-digit-length pattern, '0001-1010'), or is there an additional 1-character overhead this analysis has not identified?

BR-263-5 (excluded from the AI Solution's own SEG-120 bucket, tagged UNASSIGNED) describes the '\' line-delimiter convention used only for Blackhawk phone activation/recharge receipt text. Should the envelope validator check for well-formed '\' delimiters inside Print Data, or is that content-specific business logic that belongs to a separate Blackhawk/loyalty module, analogous to how Segment 111 leaves Appendix I Table-ID content out of its envelope scope?
provisionalItems.decision: Kept out of scope: Print Data's '\' delimiter is treated as opaque text by the envelope validator. Revisit if real (non-synthetic) data suggests delimiter well-formedness needs enforcement.

provisionalItems.question: Neither the extracted spec text nor the AI-generated requirements state whether Segment 120 may appear more than once per response message. Should cardinality be constrained to exactly one occurrence (by analogy to the confirmed Segment 101 rule SEG101-R-026), or left unconstrained until confirmed?
provisionalItems.decision: Left unconstrained for now: the validator does not cap Segment 120 occurrences at one. Revisit if real data suggests a cardinality limit is required.
